system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: L-shaped polygon]

What is the area, in square cm, of the figure shown above?

Figure, described in words:
An L-shaped polygon with six sides. The leftmost vertical side is labeled 8 cm. The bottom horizontal side is labeled 12 cm. From the top-left vertex, a horizontal top edge extends to the right to meet a vertical segment that goes downward, labeled 3 cm. From the bottom of that 3 cm segment, a horizontal edge labeled 9 cm extends to the right to meet the rightmost vertical side. Right-angle symbols are marked at five vertices: the top-left vertex, the vertex where the top horizontal edge meets the 3 cm vertical segment, the vertex where the 9 cm segment meets the right vertical side, the bottom-right vertex, and the bottom-left vertex.

A. 66
B. 69
C. 81
D. 96

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking:
I'm setting up coordinates for this L-shaped polygon, placing the bottom-left corner at the origin and working out the other vertices from the given side lengths of 8, 12, 3, and 9 cm.

Computing the area as the full 12×8 rectangle minus the 9×3 rectangle removed from the top-right corner gives 96-27=69 cm². I verify this by splitting the shape into a 12×5 bottom rectangle plus a 3×3 piece on the left, confirming 69 as the answer.
